With evolving needs of our public officers and changing procurement landscape, MOF is embarking on the Whole of Government Procurement initiative. GeBIZ X is the MOF product that would transform the procurement and business experience for WOG public officers and external suppliers. Our team is made up of passionate individuals committed to solving challenges and driving meaningful change. We embrace diversity of thought, encourage experimentation, and foster a culture of continuous learning. As part of this team, you will lead design direction and collaborate with UX designers, finance officers, and solution providers — forward-thinking professionals equally invested in your growth and in transforming MOF’s corporate finance services. We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Lead Designer to lead our product team. This individual will play a pivotal role in shaping the vision, strategy, and execution of GeBIZ X product portfolio. The Lead Designer will collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive product innovation, ensure market fit, and deliver exceptional value to our customers. The Lead Designer leads strategic design initiatives while ensuring alignment with organizational goals. He/She coordinates and plans discovery research, including user interviews, workshops, surveys, usability testing, and gathering insights to understand user needs and pain points; evaluates the usability of new and existing products and makes constructive suggestions for change. Key responsibilities include translating discovery research into actionable insights, creating wireframes and prototypes in Figma, conducting user testing, iterating designs based on feedback, and collaborating closely with product manager, software engineer to deliver user-centric solutions within technical constraints. Define and Drive Procurement Design Strategy, Roadmap, and Outcomes Develop and own the design vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for end-to-end procurement systems, aligned with MOF's digitalisation priorities. Establish, track, and deliver on design OKRs and success metrics that drive user adoption, operational impact, and continuous improvement. Prioritise design initiatives that maximise value creation and usability for procurement stakeholders, from requisition through contract management and vendor relations. Enhance Procurement Operations through Human-Centred Design and Systems Thinking Strengthen procurement workflows by embedding user research and data-driven design decisions to support strategic sourcing, vendor evaluation, and contract lifecycle management. Redesign procurement interfaces and experiences through systematic design standards that enable intuitive, multi-stakeholder collaboration across complex technology solutions (eg. SaaS/ Bespoke). Implement design systems and methodologies that proactively identify user friction points and reduce operational risk through detection of usability barriers in procurement processes. Coach and Develop the Procurement Design Practice Mentor and develop designers and design researchers to build internal capabilities and foster a high-performance, user-focused design culture. Promote cross-functional collaboration between design, product, and engineering teams whilst evangelising design-led problem-solving across the finance and digital teams. Lead the development of design standards, frameworks, and measurement methodologies that demonstrate design impact beyond traditional product metrics in complex government procurement contexts. Required qualifications, skills and mindset: Bachelor’s degree in Industrial design, Interaction design, Human Computer Interaction (HCI), Visual Arts or similar; Master’s degree preferred. Minimum of 8 years of experience in design across multiple industries, with demonstrated success in launching and scaling complex digital products. Strategic design thinking with strong analytical and synthetic capabilities, including the ability to navigate ambiguity and drive design initiatives that align with organisational objectives. Experience with agile methodologies and full product lifecycle management, particularly in complex enterprise software environments. Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams, translating user needs into strategic design decisions that balance business goals with user outcomes. Expert-level proficiency in design methodology with exceptional attention to detail and deep understanding of how users engage with complex digital systems. Advanced skills in design and research tools including Figma, Miro, and project management platforms such as Jira. Strong foundation in design principles, typography, and accessibility standards (WCAG), with experience applying these in government or regulated environments. Systems Thinking : Comfortable working across a complex organisation with diverse stakeholders and processes. Coaching & Team Growth: Skilled in mentoring others and building high-performing product teams. description: What the role is: As a Talent Acquisition Sourcer at GovTech Singapore, you will play a pivotal role in identifying and engaging top-tier tech talent to drive our mission of building Tech for Public Good. You will be a hands-on partner, focusing on the crucial initial stages of the recruitment lifecycle, and contributing to the transformation of how GovTech attracts and secures the best minds in the industry. This role requires a strategic approach to talent identification, balancing immediate hiring needs with the long-term development of our talent pipelines. This will initially start off as a 12-month contract. Talent Mapping & Market Intelligence: Conduct in-depth talent mapping exercises and gather market intelligence to understand talent landscapes, identify key organizations, and pinpoint emerging talent pools relevant to GovTech's strategic objectives. Candidate Engagement: Craft compelling outreach messages and engage potential candidates through various channels, building strong relationships and effectively communicating GovTech's value proposition and mission. Pipeline Development: Proactively build and nurture robust talent pipelines for both immediate hiring needs and future critical roles, ensuring a continuous flow of qualified candidates. Collaboration & Partnership: Work closely with Talent Acquisition Partners and hiring managers to understand specific role requirements, team dynamics, and strategic priorities, translating these into effective sourcing plans. Process Optimization: Contribute to the continuous improvement of sourcing processes, tools, and systems, leveraging data and insights to enhance efficiency, candidate experience, and overall recruitment effectiveness. Employer Branding: Act as an ambassador for GovTech, promoting our unique culture, values (Agile, Bold, Collaborative), and the impact of working on projects that serve the public good. Technical Acumen: A strong understanding of various tech domains and roles (e.g., software development, product management, design, data engineering, cybersecurity etc) to effectively identify and assess relevant talent. Communication & Influence: Excellent communication, interpersonal, and negotiation skills, with the ability to build rapport quickly and influence potential candidates. Stakeholder Management: Experience working effectively with hiring managers and internal stakeholders, providing insights and guiding them through the sourcing process. Tool Proficiency: Proficiency in using various sourcing tools and platforms, including LinkedIn Recruiter, applicant tracking systems (ATS), and other online databases and social media channels. Data-Driven Approach: A commitment to using data and metrics to inform sourcing strategies, track performance, and report on key talent insights. Alignment with GovTech Values: A genuine interest in GovTech's mission of Tech for Public Good and an embodiment of our Agile, Bold, and Collaborative values. Project Management Skills: Ability to lead or contribute to projects aimed at enhancing recruitment efficiency and candidate experience. Join us in shaping Singapore's digital future!

jobTitle: Head, Building & Infrastructure, Central Procurement Office
snippet: • Design and implement strategic procurement and contracting strategies to meet desired outcomes in supporting MHA’s and HTX’s operations. • Work closely…
responsibilities: • Design and implement strategic procurement and contracting strategies to meet desired outcomes in supporting MHA’s and HTX’s operations. • Work closely with the Project Management Teams (PMTs) or users from Home Team Departments (HTDs) and HTX Functions to provide professional advice on building projects and facility management services procurement including design of tender and specifications, and evaluation approach to maximise flexibility and staging for favourable tender outcomes. • Provide advice and support for contract management practices. • Collaborate with the HTDs and HTX Functions to analyse HTD and HTX procurement data, costs drivers, operational needs, industry factors, and conduct inter-departmental joint review of common requirements to drive demand aggregation initiatives and develop the most appropriate procurement strategy. • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including PMTs, Legal and Finance to ensure governance in procurement processes. • Provide input on procurement planning, prioritisation of projects (high complexity and value) for management reporting. • Capture lessons learnt as case studies including good practices and irregularities and present for sharing and learning. • Supervise a team of Procurement Specialists in carrying out the procurement function (from preparing tender documents to contract award), and to ensure timeliness of procurement and contract formation. • Review and assess team members’ workload and coach them for professional development. • Stay up to date with market trends and advancements; costs and performance and their applications to HTDs and HTX Functions. Observe, evaluate related market trends and development, cost and performance and recommend their applications to HTDs/HTX procurements in terms of desired KPI, cost and efficiency (e.g., impact of pandemic-related expenses and construction material price impacts). • Negotiates with suppliers for strategic buys and establishment of master agreements/enterprise agreements to achieve cost effective outcomes and favourable terms and conditions for MHA and HTX.
requirements: •Possess a degree preferably with at least 8 years of relevant experience in areas of procurement ranging from acquisition of services, strategic sourcing, integrated workforce and public private partnership, preferably in the Public Built Environment Sector. •Excellent knowledge of procurement strategies, procedures, standards and guidelines specified in the Government Instruction Manual on Procurement, Finance Circulars and existing rules and regulations • Good knowledge of strategic sourcing, project management and demand aggregation activities. • Keen interest in developing knowledge and enhancing competency in the respective teams. • Able to work in a dynamic fast paced environment and manage workload well. • Strong analytical and communication skills • Must be able to work well in a team. • Min 3 years of supervisory experience in leading a team. All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement. #LI-CW1

agency: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX)
jobTitle: Head, Building & Infrastructure, Central Procurement Office
snippet: • Design and implement strategic procurement and contracting strategies to meet desired outcomes in supporting MHA’s and HTX’s operations. • Work closely…
responsibilities: • Design and implement strategic procurement and contracting strategies to meet desired outcomes in supporting MHA’s and HTX’s operations. • Work closely with the Project Management Teams (PMTs) or users from Home Team Departments (HTDs) and HTX Functions to provide professional advice on building projects and facility management services procurement including design of tender and specifications, and evaluation approach to maximise flexibility and staging for favourable tender outcomes. • Provide advice and support for contract management practices. • Collaborate with the HTDs and HTX Functions to analyse HTD and HTX procurement data, costs drivers, operational needs, industry factors, and conduct inter-departmental joint review of common requirements to drive demand aggregation initiatives and develop the most appropriate procurement strategy. • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including PMTs, Legal and Finance to ensure governance in procurement processes. • Provide input on procurement planning, prioritisation of projects (high complexity and value) for management reporting. • Capture lessons learnt as case studies including good practices and irregularities and present for sharing and learning. • Supervise a team of Procurement Specialists in carrying out the procurement function (from preparing tender documents to contract award), and to ensure timeliness of procurement and contract formation. • Review and assess team members’ workload and coach them for professional development. • Stay up to date with market trends and advancements; costs and performance and their applications to HTDs and HTX Functions. Observe, evaluate related market trends and development, cost and performance and recommend their applications to HTDs/HTX procurements in terms of desired KPI, cost and efficiency (e.g., impact of pandemic-related expenses and construction material price impacts). • Negotiates with suppliers for strategic buys and establishment of master agreements/enterprise agreements to achieve cost effective outcomes and favourable terms and conditions for MHA and HTX.
requirements: •Possess a degree preferably with at least 8 years of relevant experience in areas of procurement ranging from acquisition of services, strategic sourcing, integrated workforce and public private partnership, preferably in the Public Built Environment Sector. •Excellent knowledge of procurement strategies, procedures, standards and guidelines specified in the Government Instruction Manual on Procurement, Finance Circulars and existing rules and regulations • Good knowledge of strategic sourcing, project management and demand aggregation activities. • Keen interest in developing knowledge and enhancing competency in the respective teams. • Able to work in a dynamic fast paced environment and manage workload well. • Strong analytical and communication skills • Must be able to work well in a team. • Min 3 years of supervisory experience in leading a team. All new hires are appointed on a two-year contract in the first instance and will be assessed and considered for permanent tenure over time, based on performance. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks upon closing of the advertisement. #LI-CW1
